source_title: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook: Construction and Building Inspectors
observation: BLS reports 147,600 jobs in the broad occupation in 2024, 5% self-employed, and describes home inspectors doing daytime inspections and sometimes writing reports in the evening.
limitations: Occupation includes inspectors outside residential home-purchase inspection.
Employment is not the addressable paid iOS user count.

source_title: HomeGauge Companion US App Store listing and reviews
observation: Reviewed public comments describe mobile reporting removing substantial post-inspection desk work while another current user reports camera reliability problems during daily field use.
denominator: two inspected public review examples from a listing with 39 ratings
limitations: Review statements were not independently verified.

observation: Spectora publicly lists a recurring home-inspection software offer at $109 per month or $1,090 per year.
limitations: List price is not transaction or retention evidence.
Payment is primarily web SaaS, not Apple IAP.
Spectora and HomeGauge share an ownership root after the 2026 acquisition.

observation: RevenueCat reports Business category median D60 revenue per install of $0.50 and that 75.1% of North American projects obtain more than 80% of revenue from the App Store.
unit: USD median D60 RPI, Business category
denominator: RevenueCat-integrated subscription apps included in the 2026 report
limitations: Not US-only, inspector-specific, or an Apple-IAP-only population.
Benchmark is not first-party economics for this idea.

source_title: HomeGauge Companion US App Store field-workflow reviews
observation: The same review set shows value from mobile placement into an existing report workflow and pain from camera reliability, supporting a narrow reliable capture/export wedge rather than another full suite.
limitations: The wedge is an inference from a small self-selected sample.
No switching or payment behavior for the proposed companion was observed.

observation: ASHI requires a written inspection report and leaves professional observations and judgments with the inspector, supporting a source-linked draft and mandatory human-approval scope.
limitations: ASHI is not a substitute for state-by-state legal review.
The standard does not validate the proposed product.

observation: Apple permits auto-renewable subscriptions across app categories and requires privacy, consent, data minimization, security, and disclosure when personal data is shared with third-party AI.
limitations: Guidelines are a compliance path, not approval assurance.

observation: The public occupation table does not isolate active US independent residential home-purchase inspectors who use iPhone and paid report software.
limitations: Only broader occupation and membership proxies are available.
